test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is correct if the egg is NOT fertilised with the sperm?

options.text: Uterus lining slowly breaks, sheds as blood and mucous
Uterus lining becomes thick and spongy

solution:
The correct answer is __**Uterus lining slowly breaks, sheds as blood and mucous**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an **egg** (ovum) is released during **ovulation** and is **not fertilized** by a **sperm**, the high levels of **progesterone** and **estrogen** required to maintain the **pregnancy** environment begin to drop.
 
• The **uterus lining** (endometrium) does not simply become thin; rather, it undergoes a programmed breakdown because the hormonal support from the **corpus luteum** is withdrawn. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **uterus lining slowly breaks** down and is discharged through the **vagina**. This discharge consists of **blood**, **mucous**, and **endometrial tissue**, a process known as **menstruation**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The **uterus lining** is significantly affected by the lack of **fertilization**; it cannot remain "unaffected" as the body must reset the cycle for a new **egg** release. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• While the **uterus lining becomes thick and spongy** during the **secretory phase** (after **ovulation**) to prepare for a potential **embryo**, this occurs **before** the determination of non-fertilization. Once it is clear no fertilization occurred, this thick lining is shed. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The average **menstrual cycle** lasts for about **28 days**, and the bleeding phase (menstruation) typically lasts for **3 to 7 days**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Phases of the Menstrual Cycle:**

 
 
• **Menstrual Phase:** This is the first phase where the **endometrium** is shed if fertilization has not occurred. It marks the start of the cycle (**Day 1**).
 
• **Follicular Phase:** This phase overlaps with the menstrual phase and continues until **ovulation**. The **Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH)** stimulates the **ovaries** to produce follicles.
 
• **Ovulatory Phase:** Around **day 14** of a **28-day** cycle, a surge in **Luteinizing Hormone (LH)** triggers the release of a mature **egg** from the **ovary**.
 
• **Luteal Phase:** After **ovulation**, the ruptured follicle transforms into the **corpus luteum**, which secretes **progesterone** to keep the **uterine lining** thick. If **fertilization** does not occur, the **corpus luteum** withers away.
 
 
 
• **Key Hormones involved:**
 
 
• **Estrogen:** Responsible for rebuilding the **uterine lining** after **menstruation**.
 
• **Progesterone:** Known as the **pregnancy hormone**, it maintains the **thick and spongy** nature of the **endometrium**.
 
• **FSH and LH:** Pituitary hormones that regulate the maturation of the **egg** and the timing of **ovulation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Menarche:** This term refers to the **first menstrual period** in a female's life, typically occurring between the ages of **10 and 15**.
 
• **Menopause:** This is the biological stage marking the end of **menstrual cycles**, usually diagnosed after a woman has gone **12 months** without a period, typically occurring between **45 and 55 years** of age.
 
• **Fertilization:** This process usually occurs in the **Fallopian tube** (Ampulla). If it occurs, the **zygote** travels to the **uterus** for **implantation**, and the **menstrual cycle** stops during the **9 months** of **gestation**.
 
• **Corpus Albicans:** If fertilization does not take place, the **corpus luteum** degenerates into a white fibrous tissue called the **corpus albicans**, leading to the drop in **progesterone** that triggers **menstruation**.
